The coupled BEM-CFD model is computationally efficient compared to transient CFD simulations of rotating blades, allowing it to simulate larger numbers of turbines in an array.
Wake recovery to free-stream conditions downstream of a single turbine was found to be independent of the inlet flow velocity.
The minimum velocity observed downstream of a single turbine was between 37.8% and 39.3% of the inlet velocity, occurring 2.0 diameters downstream of the rotor.
By 40 diameters downstream of a single turbine, the velocity had recovered to around 92% of the inlet velocity magnitude.

For a longitudinally aligned pair of turbines, the performance of the downstream rotor improved significantly with increasing the longitudinal distance between the rotors, even when the spacing was 40 diameters.
For a longitudinal spacing of 10 diameters between a pair of turbines, the power output of the downstream rotor was only 29.3% of the upstream rotor, compared to 82.8% for a 40 diameter spacing.

Increasing the lateral spacing between a pair of turbines to 4.0 diameters or greater resulted in flow acceleration between them, with velocities up to 4% higher than the freestream velocity observed 40 diameters downstream.
For a low lateral spacing between a pair of turbines (3 diameters or less), flow recovery was slow between them because of wake expansion.

The authors were able to optimize the layout of a 14-turbine staggered array based on the patterns observed for two and three turbine arrangements, increasing the total power output by over 10% compared to a regular staggered configuration.
The authors calculated turbulence intensity from the predicted velocity and turbulent kinetic energy using the formula T_i = (2k/3)^0.5/U.
The authors used a variable resolution grid to evaluate the velocity and turbulence characteristics downstream of the turbines, with finer resolution near the turbines and wake regions.
The blade-box region containing the turbine rotor was modeled using a structured mesh with a resolution of 64 x 64 x 10 elements and cell sizes of 0.2 m x 0.2 m x 0.1 m.
An unstructured mesh was used in the upstream and downstream regions of the domain, with maximum element sizes ranging from 0.5 m to 4.0 m depending on the distance from the turbine.

The authors validated the BEM-CFD model against experimental data, with discrepancies in the predicted power coefficients compared to the experiment ranging from -1.07% to 7.95% for tip speed ratios between 4.0 and 8.0.

The authors also validated the model's ability to predict velocity structures in the wake regions downstream of turbine rotors, with maximum errors of 11.38% observed along the mid-wake of any of the rotors.
